name: Scrap-Sirocco

civilization.name: Vantage Clans
civilization.notes: Nomadic scavenger tribes descended from the dreadnought's ground crew, living within the wreck's pressurized gun decks and worshipping the ship as an ancestor-god.

specific_features: Starship crash site: the fleet dreadnought Vantage lies half-buried bow-down in the deep dunes of the Marrow Waste, downed on the final day of the Unification Wars, her twelve-kilometer hull now a wind-carved canyon of gun decks and sealed compartments.
Smuggler cache: a hidden supply vault in the Vantage's reactor section is restocked every few months by parties unknown, containing parts the Clans' own technology could not manufacture.

Signal of unknown origin: on nights after sandstorms, a repeating transmission rises from the sealed command deck—old fleet cipher, sender designation belonging to an admiral recorded as dead before the battle.
description: Rust-orange dunes march to every horizon under a sky the color of old bronze, broken only by the mountain ranges at the equator and the vast dark hump of the Vantage rising from the sands. Sheets of impact glass spread for hundreds of kilometers where orbital fire slagged the desert on the war's last day. When the sirocco winds rise, they hiss through the wreck's open gun ports and moan down her corridors like a crew at work.

Days scorch and nights freeze, and the Clans move with them, sleeping in the hull's insulated magazines by night and working the shadowed decks by day. The air inside the wreck tastes of machine oil and hot iron, a smell the tribes consider sacred. Sand sings against everything, forever polishing the bones of the ship thinner.

The Vantage died leading the loyalist fleet at the Battle of the Marrow, and her captain sealed the command deck as the ship fell, taking the fleet logs with it. The scavenger clans who descend from her surviving ground crew have made a religion of her passages, but they do not enter the command deck; their oldest law forbids waking what sleeps there. After storms, however, something on that deck transmits in a dead admiral's voice.

Offworld salvage consortiums covet the uranium still stacked in the Vantage's magazines and the secrets sealed behind the command deck's blast doors. The smugglers who quietly restock the reactor cache want something from inside as well, and the Clans have begun finding their offerings moved rather than taken. Every faction converging on the desert agrees on one thing: whoever opens the command deck first will learn who sold the fleet—and the answer was worth killing a world for.
